definition_summary: Let G=Gal(C/R). The restriction of alpha in H_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)) to X(R), followed by the canonical map(1.57), has components alpha_p for p congruent to k modulo2. The topological subgroup0 is defined by alpha_{k+i}=Sq^i(alpha_k) for even i, with negative squares zero. For1-cycles on a D-dimensional variety, k=D-1 and Remark1.20(i) equivalently requires alpha_p=0 for p<k. Over real numbers, Hdg_G0 intersects this subgroup with the inverse image of ordinary Hodge(k,k) classes. RIHC means surjectivity of CH^k(X) to Hdg_G0. PartII keeps its stated scope R=real numbers or H^2(O_X)=0.
